This indicates that the compound may act through a common mechanism that affects HaCaT cells. The evidence suggests that the compound may inhibit HaCaT cells through a pathway involving cell cycle regulation or other cellular processes, as these targets are known to influence cell proliferation and differentiation. The presence of multiple targets and the consistent relationship across different pathways support the hypothesis that the compound exerts its effect on HaCaT cells through a well-defined mechanism.
